 Judgment
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned Advocates appearing for both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
2. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that:
On 21.03.2012 at about 9.30 a.m. deceased along with his friend while they were near the Kandoor bus stand the respondent No.1 came with his vehicle bearing registration No.KA.19/EE 4574 in high speed and rash and negligent manner and hit the backside of Basavaraja @ Durgappa @ Durganna, resulting in claimant sustaining grievous injuries.

Later on he was shifted to A J Hospital Institute of Medical Science, Mangalore and during the treatment the said Basavaraj @
Durgappa succumbed to injuries.

entities.text: J Hospital Institute of Medical Science, Mangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Due to his death, the petitioners have lost their beloved family member, who was the only earning member of the family.

Therefore,
the claimants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
claiming compensation of Rs.22,00,000/-.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that Tribunal has not properly awarded the compensation in accordance with law.
The accident is of the year 2012 and the deceased was the driver of Tata Hitachi and he was earning salary of Rs.15,000/- per month as per Ex. P-5.
The Tribunal has considered Rs.5,000/- as monthly income, which is meager.
The deceased was a skilled labour and he was aged less than 40 years.
The Tribunal has also not awarded any amount towards loss of future prospects of the deceased.
On all these grounds, sought for allowing this appeal by enhancing the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
5. As against this, learned counsel for the respondent has submitted his arguments that Tribunal has passed the impugned judgment and award in accordance with law.
That there are no grounds to interfere with the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
On all these grounds, sought for dismissal of the appeal.

2 6. On hearing the arguments and on perusal of records, following points would arise for consideration:
(1) Whether the appellants have made out a ground to interfere with the impugned judgment and award as to the quantum of compensation?
(2) What order?
7.

A perusal of impugned judgment and award reveals that in para 15 the Tribunal has observed as under:
"Issue No.3:- Petitioner deposed in her evidence her son was resided in Mangalore and working as Hitachi operator and he was getting monthly income of Rs.15,000/-
and she has produced evidence of PW.2, PW.2 is one Yalgurdappa, has deposed he is the owner of the Hitachi, in it deceased was working as Hitachi Operator and he is paying monthly salary of Rs.15,000/-, he has produced Ex.P.9 based on the Ex.P.9 petitioner prays to direct the respondent to pay the compensation amount of Rs.22,00,000/-. Petitioner No.2 deposed in his evidence he is having Hitachi.
But on going through the evidence of PW.2, he is also originally belongs to Hadalgeri village and deceased was belongs to same village and he is residing at Sulya since 12 years..

In order prove this contention petitioner No.2 has not placed any voter card or adhar card and other document to hold that he was residing at Sulya and he has produced Ex.P.9 it does not bears EST & CST and he has not produced he is paying income tax,
when he is having Hitachi and he has paying monthly salary of Rs.15,000/- then he ought to make payment of income tax but in this regard his evidence is not sufficient to hold that he has paying salary of RS.15,000/- to the deceased.
It seems PW No.2 and deceased are belongs to same village.
Normally, a person may get salary when he was working Hitachi Operator or other vehicle therefore, this tribunal has taken his income of Rs.5000/- per month and deceased was aged about 19 years.

On going through the Ex.P.5 deceased was aged about 19 years due to multiple injuries he succumbed such being the case this court relied on the judgement of Hon'ble supreme court of India Judgement reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 SARALA VARMA AND OTHERS V/S DELHI TRANSPORTATION AND ANOTHER, according to the Hon'ble Supreme Court judgement multiplier 18 is applicable therefore his income is t a k e n R s . 5 0 0 0 / - , h i s p e r s o n a l e x p e n s e s t o b e d e d u c t e d 5 0 0 0 x 2 - 2500x12x18-5,40,000/-,

sentences.text: In this petition deceased got un-married therefore, half of the personal expenses is deducted and I award Rs.5,40,000/- towards loss of dependency.

towards funeral expenses therefore, petitioners are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.6,05,000/- with 6% future interest under the following heads : which comes Loss of dependency Rs.5,40,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs. 20,000/-

Respondent has produced insurance policy and he has taken contention that said vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 then respondent No.2 is contractual liable to pay the compensation amount to said petitioners accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 in Partly Affirmative."
8. Ex.P-9 is the salary certificate issued by the owner of Bharat Earth Movers, District Mangaluru.
The owner of the Bharat Earth Movers is examined as PW2.
Salary certificate reveals that owner of this vehicle was paying Rs.15,000/- per month.

The Tribunal has not assigned any proper reasons to reject this salary certificate issued by the owner, but the owner has not produced any receipts as to the payment of this salary to the deceased but admittedly he is a Hitachi driver.
9. However, considering the occupation of the deceased it is just and proper to assess the income of the claimant at Rs.8,000/- per month.

Since the claimant is aged 19 years, in view of decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE CO., LTD., VS. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157 and MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. NANU RAM ALIAS CHUHRU RAM & OTHERS reported in 2018 ACJ 2782, 40% has to be added towards future prospects to the income, which would result in Rs.11,200/- (Rs.8,000/-
+ 40% (Rs.5,600/-)).
10.
